extracted.intended_audience: members of princely courts; gentlemen and ladies seeking guidance on courtly conduct (readers of Renaissance etiquette)
extracted.subtask_description: A dialogic Renaissance manual describing the qualities, accomplishments, behaviour, and duties expected of a 'perfect Courtier' and of a Court Lady, and how they should employ those qualities in service of a prince. Covers personal virtues, arts, conversation, dress, duties to a prince, and limits of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentle birth
rubrics_metrics.description: Especially gentle birth is enumerated among the conditions essential to the Courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a primary social prerequisite; emphasised in early discussion of what constitutes a Courtier’s standing in court society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arms as the Courtier's true profession
rubrics_metrics.description: Arms the true profession of the Courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courtier must be skilled in martial exercises and warlike duties but this skill must be exercised without arrogance or boasting; arms contrasted repeatedly with letters/arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical qualities and martial exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical qualities and martial exercises are essential accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes training in riding, vaulting on horseback, wrestling, swimming, weapons handling and other military exercises appropriate to a gentleman; to be practised so the Courtier may serve in war and public contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace (sprezzatura/nonchalance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grace — an easy, graceful demeanour — is an essential quality of the Courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasised repeatedly (including notion of sprezzatura): accomplishments should be shown with apparent ease and avoidance of awkwardness or ostentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid affectation in behaviour and speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courtier should be natural and not affected; affectation is condemned for both men and women and in arts, dress, and conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary and conversational style
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary and conversational style is a key accomplishment for the Courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courtier should be able to converse well, with good taste, variety, and adequacy to company; includes knowledge of literature, ability to use vernacular, and rules for speaking and writing governed by same principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music as an accomplishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Music is one of the Courtier's accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different kinds of music have appropriate times for practice and display; aged courtiers should avoid public musical performance; music is weighed against other arts in usefulness and decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting and sculpture knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarity with painting (and comparison of painting vs. sculpture) is presented as part of the Courtier's cultural accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courtier should appreciate and discuss visual arts intelligently; the text supplies comparisons and guidance on when and how to speak of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dancing and masquerading
rubrics_metrics.description: Dancing (and masquerading) are proper exercises for the Courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dancing is an appropriate evening entertainment and social skill; its public performance should be sensitive to age and occasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical use/time of accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for the way and time of employing the Courtier's qualities and accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rules: avoid affectation, speak and act discreetly and opportunely; employ accomplishments to seek honour and praise in appropriate contests; know when to display abilities and when to refrain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation with respect to age
rubrics_metrics.description: Aged Courtiers should moderate youthful pursuits; youthful Courtiers should moderate faults peculiar to their age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elder courtiers should avoid public music/dancing and temper pursuits unsuitable for their years; youths should restrain excesses and be mindful of appropriate behaviour for age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversation with superiors; winning favour worthily
rubrics_metrics.description: How to converse with social superiors and how to win favours worthily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises tact, discretion, modesty, readiness, and timing in addressing superiors; instructs on avoiding flattery and using speech to gain honour without indecorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress and ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice and moderation of dress and ornament are important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dress must suit station and occasion; fashions are discussed critically (some fashions lamented); sumptuary restraint and tasteful attire are commended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and treatment of friends
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful choice and treatment of friends is advised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsels judicious friendships, loyalty, and use of friends for reputation and support; warns against indiscriminate or dishonourable associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate pastimes and games
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain pastimes (cards, chess, tennis, venery, etc.) are appropriate to the Courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pastimes are useful for training and diversion but should be moderated; some games praised (chess) while gambling or excess is warned against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation and first impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Influence of preconceived opinions and first impressions; advantage of being preceded by a good reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reputation helps, the Courtier should not rely solely on it; good conduct should back reputation; be mindful of how first impressions affect treatment by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tact, modesty, kindness, readiness; seizing opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Tact, modesty, kindness, readiness; and taking advantage of opportunities are core behavioural virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These qualities enable the Courtier to be useful and esteemed; includes advice on judicious self-presentation and responsiveness in company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confession of ignorance
rubrics_metrics.description: Confession of ignorance when appropriate is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better to confess lack of knowledge than to feign; honesty in conversation increases credibility and avoids affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-depreciation and self-praise boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on self-depreciation and self-praise: avoid excesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-depreciation and boasting are both dangerous; maintain a balanced humility appropriate to station and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasantries and witticisms (timeliness and discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of pleasantries and witticisms governed by timeliness and discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wit is valuable but must be used opportunely and without malice; avoid going beyond bounds in the effort to amuse; rules and examples are discussed at length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical jokes and trickery in love — use discreetly
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical jokes and trickery (especially in matters of love) may be used but with discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical jokes should be employed discreetly, particularly around women; artifice in love is described but dignity and nobility should not be compromised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity and nobility of women
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect for the dignity and nobility of women is insisted upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women’s honour and status are to be preserved; admonitions against scandal-mongering and indecorous behaviour toward women run throughout the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court Lady: affability, modesty, decorum
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court Lady should be affable, modest, and decorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: She must follow a middle course between prudishness and over-freedom, avoid scandal-mongering, and cultivate variety in conversation and graceful demeanour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court Lady: accomplishments, dress, chastity, conduct in love
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court Lady’s physical and mental exercises, dress, demeanour in love, chastity and continence are treated as defining qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples and counsels on how a lady should win and keep love, maintain secrecy where required, and preserve virtue and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Courtier's duty to his prince: instruct and inform truthfully
rubrics_metrics.description: The Courtier's relations with his prince should aim to lead the prince to good and to inform him of truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courtier must employ his qualities so the prince may be led to seek good and shun evil; duty includes courage to tell the truth and give wise counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue can be cultivated; temperance as chief virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is not wholly innate but susceptible of cultivation; temperance is the perfect virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on moral education: training by habit and confirmation by reason; temperance regarded as the fountain of other virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes of a good prince (context for the Courtier's service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes of a good prince: justice, devoutness, love of his subjects, and mild sway; princes should avoid extremes and attend to details personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides how the Courtier should train and serve princes, advocate for peace as aim of war, and recommend virtues befitting rulers; public works and prudent governance praised.
